fixes.explanation: Manna. The crowd says, "Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness…" They bring it up right after asking, "What sign then will You perform, so that we may see it and believe You?" (John 6:30). I think they're hoping Jesus will top that menu.

Reward is a fair guess, but Jesus doesn't say it here. He says He will lose none of those the Father gave Him, "…but raise them up at the last day." Nobody has to earn a spot first. I've been the forgotten one in the back of a drawer, so a promise that none get lost hits me right in the apron.

Teaching is a good thought, but Jesus doesn't use that word here. He says, "And this bread, which I will give for the life of the world, is My flesh." Notice what He's giving: Himself, not just something to learn. I bet that's why the crowd in the synagogue started arguing among themselves (John 6:52).
